# open_kernels working notes (verbatim from project memory)

- **0a toolchain**: mlir-aie 1.4.2 + Peano build xclbins in WSL
  (`~/ironenv142`, `~/mlir-aie` at tag v1.4.2). `xclbinutil` + `aiebu-asm`
  are NOT in the wheel and WSL has no sudo — built from XRT master in a
  Docker `ubuntu:24.04` container into `~/xrt-tools/{bin,lib}`
  (recipe: scratchpad build_xclbinutil.sh). Build a design with
  `tools/open-kernels/build_design.py` (@iron.jit) or `build_mlir.sh` (raw
  MLIR). Our own kernels run through phlegm's driver: ROT13 byte-exact.
- **0b expert fetch**: a shim DMA descriptor into a big DDR pool, retargeted
  to a runtime-chosen slab and enqueued by CONTROL PACKETS with no host
  round-trip. Array->shim-control directly does not deliver (AIE2 target
  model); bounce the packet words through DDR (S2MM out, shim MM2S back into
  its own TileControl) — a legal flow, and how FLM does it (its shim BDs
  4-7/12-15 are written-but-never-enqueued by the txn stream; 32 = 8 experts
  x 4 stripes). Proof: designs/expert_fetch/ddr_bounce_fetch.mlir, idx 3/7
  give exact per-slab sums.

## Prefill chunk size

- `--prefill-chunk-len` sets how many tokens one prefill chunk holds; the docs give a default of 4096. (cli.md:299-313)
- In code a user value below 512 is raised to 512. Without the flag FLM takes the model's `max_prefill_len` from `model_list.json`, which is 4096 for all 35 entries, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B included; the last fallback is also 4096. (runner.cpp:83-92, rest_handler.cpp:334-337, 414-415)
- This answers the chunk size the 2026-09-01 engine captures could not find ("Prefill chunk 1/1 with N tokens").

- The closed engine's fixed prefill term moved between 9.93, 10.0, 12.1 and 14.8 s across fits (marginal rate stable at ~264-280 tok/s); its run-to-run spread at one length was 48-158 tok/s, so the open/closed crossover reads ~1700, ~3100, ~3600-3700 or "past 4800" tokens depending on the run.

- The plans first credited the in-binary PASSIVE setting for 38.55 -> 29.93 s at 2582 tokens; the 09-21 notes show it never applied and the gain came from setting the variable in the shell.

Host "hipx": Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (MS-S1 MAX), Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic (2026-09-16) then 7.0.0-38-generic (2026-10-02), in-tree amdxdna (DRM driver 0.7.0), NPU 1022:17f0 rev 0x11 "RyzenAI-npu5", firmware 1.1.2.65 (`amdnpu/17f0_11/npu_7.sbin`), iommu=pt (identity domain), HIP 7.15.26333 / ROCm core 10.0.0, gfx1151 iGPU; XRT 2.21.75 installed but not used by this path. A second Strix Halo box "halo" ran Linux 7.2 (firmware not stated) for commit a053503c8. No Windows.

## Raw dispatch without XRT

- A libc-only path ran mlir-aie PDIs and instruction streams bit-exact against XRT, also after context destroy/recreate: 64 MiB DEV_HEAP BO at a 64 MiB-aligned host VA, CREATE_HWCTX (all-zero QoS, max_opc 2048, num_tiles 32), DEV BO for the PDI, CONFIG_HWCTX CU (16 B payload), DEV BO for the instructions, SHMEM BOs for data, one CMD BO, EXEC_CMD, then `DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_TIMELINE_WAIT` (WAIT_FOR_SUBMIT) on the hwctx syncobj at the EXEC_CMD seq, then a check for ERT state 4.
- The working ERT_START_CU packet: header `0x30010001`, cu_mask 1, payload opcode 3, instruction address, instruction size in bytes (not words), then bo0..bo4. bo0 sits at payload offset 0x14, so the u64 slots are 4-mod-8 unaligned.
- Kernel 7.0 has no WAIT_CMD ioctl. The syncobj timeline wait works instead.
- `SYNC_BO FROM_DEVICE` returns EINVAL for SHMEM BOs on this driver; `TO` works. Readback uses CPU `clflush` per 64 B line with `mfence` before and after. The source says this matches the installed XRT shim's default non-coherent sync (`clflush_data`).
- The output buffer must also be flushed before the run, so a later dirty-line eviction cannot overwrite device output.
- The readback flush averaged 1.475 ms for a 35.65 MB GEMM output and 17.345 µs for a 524,288 B output (all iterations).
- Only bo0..bo4 reach the firmware, so every design uses at most 5 DDR-patched buffers. Consistent with F-0012.

## GPU buffer imports (gfx1151 iGPU)

- `SYNC_BO` on an imported dma-buf handle oopses the kernel (7.0.0-31). Imported buffers use CPU flush only. The command BO must be of CMD type.
- XDNA→XDNA PRIME import ran correctly, but mmap of the imported BO returned EINVAL, and importer-side sync or a direct dma-buf mmap killed the probe session.
- NPU→GPU import fails: KFD rejects dma-bufs that amdgpu did not export (`amdgpu_amdkfd_get_dmabuf_info`).
- GPU `hipMalloc` buffers imported into amdxdna were read and written bit-exactly by an NPU kernel (control 6/6, read 12/12, write 36/36). Import setup took 0.8-3.9 ms, once.
- A HIP VMM host allocation exported with `hipMemGetHandleForAddressRange` aliases only bytes written before the export. After the amdxdna import, GPU writes do not show through the dma-buf and dma-buf writes do not reach the GPU (64 KiB to 16 MiB, pinned or uncached). This withdrew the source's 2026-10-02 "zero-copy" verdict.
- Live sharing works with anonymous host pages pinned by amdxdna as a userptr BO and `hipHostRegister`ed for the GPU. A three-way alias check (CPU, GPU kernel, NPU map) passes on it.
- All 16 page and flag mixes (4k, THP, hugetlb 2M, 1G × hipHostRegister 0 / Portable / Mapped / CoarseGrained) were accepted by amdxdna. The GPU read 238-241 GB/s and wrote 220-227 GB/s on the shared pages.
- Linux 7.2 amdxdna refuses mmap of a userptr BO with EINVAL. The caller's own map of the same pinned pages works as the CPU view (commit a053503c8).

- Linux 7.2 amdxdna refuses mmap of a userptr BO with EINVAL. The caller's own map of the same pinned pages works as the CPU view (commit a053503c8).

## CPU-free work ring

- The ring is one START_CU whose stream loops over slots. A self-looping shim BD copies the slot's `seq` word from DDR into memtile memory, and the stream MASKPOLLs that word; after the C SYNCs one 64 B DMA write posts the done line.
- With the CPU as producer: publish → done seen p50 4.5 µs (min 1.4-2.6, p99 51-73 µs on each round's first slot); done → done 5.3 µs when slots were published ahead. Paced and published-ahead runs gave the same 897 µs per GEMM slot.
- Ring plus lean streams: gate_up 29.93 busy / 29.90 wall TOPS (897 µs per slot), down 31.87 / 31.80 (421 µs).
- With the gfx1151 iGPU as producer (shared userptr pages): GPU publish → NPU done → GPU observe p50 3.13 µs (min 2.73); one uncached poll load costs 0.24 µs.
- Full GPU → NPU → GPU round trip with a 512×1280×2560 int8 GEMM per run: 271 → 128 µs per run (`--slots 8 --nslots 4 --rounds 16`: 8 runs per command over 4 ring slots; median of 3 processes; byte-exact), on the Linux 7.2 "halo" box. 512×2560×640: 164 → 113 µs. Steps: two GPU streams, lean re-arm, rounds queued one ahead, B kept resident in the memtile.

## Doubtful

- The commit title says 164 → 112 µs for the down shape; CHANGELOG.md says 113 µs.
- F-0022 found re-executed XRT runlists slower than fresh runs on FLM kernels (Windows); here retained and chained raw commands were faster than eager ones. Different stack and mechanism.
- F-0064 gives ~4 ms for a first dispatch on Strix Point/Windows; here 1.6 ms (first ring command) and ~2.5 ms (tiny GEMM after context recreate, 2026-09-16).
- Bears on Q-0005: on Linux the no-op round trip is 59 µs (20-25 µs queued), but firmware execution of the transaction stream adds roughly 150 µs per 51 KB. Stream size may explain part of the spread in per-call floors.
- Bears on Q-0006: a design switch inside one context costs ~1.0-1.2 ms per alternating submit at these sizes.
- Bears on Q-0013: on Linux/Halo one context ran 20626 submits in one loop and a 935 KB 64-expert stream with no timeout.

## Measured by ggml-xdna (WSL, 2026-10-12)

- WSL's Ubuntu 24.04 has no `/dev/accel`, the node the Linux NPU driver creates. WSL passes the GPU through (`/dev/dxg`) but not the NPU, so nothing NPU-side can be run or timed from WSL; only builds and host-only tests.

- Built against ggml-xdna's vendored XRT 2.20 headers, it ran with XRT 2.25 (headers older than runtime worked).

## OpenFlowLM, whole model on the NPU

- q4_1: prompt reading 134 / 136 / 139 / 137 tok/s.
- q4_1: reply writing (32 tokens after the prompt) 12.4 / 12.0 / 10.8 / 8.9 tok/s.
- 8-bit weights with 4-bit experts: prompt reading 112 / 116 / 118 / 114 tok/s.
- 8-bit weights with 4-bit experts: reply writing 7.0 / 8.2 / 7.8 / 6.6 tok/s.
- OpenFlowLM's reply speed drops as the prompt grows (12.4 to 8.9 tok/s from 1k to 8k), while the GPU engines hold steady (`README.md:287-288`).

## llama.cpp with the add-on (NPU matmuls, GPU for the rest)

- Q4_K_M, prompt reading: with the add-on 223 / 216 / 259 / 235; GPU alone 223 / 202 / 197 / 202. Lead of up to 1.31x.
- Q8_0, prompt reading: with the add-on 170 / 196 / 199 / 198; GPU alone 181 / 168 / 199 / 187. Lead of up to 1.17x.
- The add-on leaves replies to the GPU, so its reply rows should equal the GPU-alone rows. They differ by up to 14%; the source reads 14% as the noise on any figure in these tables (`README.md:278-280`).
- The NPU cannot take the expert step in this add-on, so only attention and shared weights reach the NPU on this model (`README.md:375-377`).
